findings.desc: missing-evidence-crash: analyze-batch.mjs main() computes generatedInputs via readFileBytes(paths.tamper) and readFileBytes(paths.resume) (plain readFileSync, no try/catch) at lines 176-177, which throws an uncaught ENOENT and exits nonzero with a raw stack trace (no report.json/report.md written, no FATAL input-integrity message) when tamper-verdicts.jsonl or resume-reconciliation.json is genuinely absent from the evidence directory. This directly contradicts the code's own documented contract one block above: the comment at lines 130-132 states tamper-verdicts.jsonl integrity is structural and 'a missing required field makes a hypothesis inconclusive, never a crash', and the comment at line 137 states 'resume-reconciliation.json: missing/empty => H3 inconclusive'. The adjudication logic (adjudicateH2/adjudicateH3) does correctly treat these files as missing via readTextOrNull => inconclusive, so the three-state adjudication itself never yields a false pass -- but the downstream report-generation step crashes before any report is emitted, an unhandled path inconsistent with the documented contract. selfcheck-m4.mjs sub-check G only exercises the present-but-EMPTY resume-reconciliation.json case (writes an empty string, not an absent file); there is no sub-check for a genuinely absent tamper-verdicts.jsonl or resume-reconciliation.json. Reproduced: copy only batch-ledger.jsonl+protocol.json(+.sha256)+lib/ into a fresh sandbox (omit tamper-verdicts.jsonl and resume-reconciliation.json) and run node analyze-batch.mjs -> throws Error: ENOENT at readFileBytes (analyze-batch.mjs:51) called from main (analyze-batch.mjs:176), exit code 1, no report.json produced.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 3e5c582a: absent input file -> the dependent hypothesis is inconclusive + generatedInputs sha null (never an uncaught crash); protocol.json absent stays hard-fatal. selfcheck-m4 sub-check O (delete tamper-verdicts.jsonl -> no crash, H2 inconclusive, overall some-inconclusive).

findings.desc: H1 false-pass: adjudicateH1 (analyze-batch.mjs:221-258) treats a scale with >=2 proof records as checkable/pass-eligible purely by record COUNT, without checking that digests/goldMetrics are actually present. If every proof record at a scale has digests+goldMetrics stripped/undefined (malformed producer output that still carries verifyStatus), canonicalJson({digests:undefined,goldMetrics:undefined}) is identical across records, so pairwiseEqual is vacuously true and H1 verdict=pass even though NO real replay-determinism evidence was compared. This can flip overall to all-pass and assert the verbatim SS3 claim on zero real evidence. Reproduced: stripped digests+goldMetrics from all 3 full-scale ledger records (recordDigest re-signed so input-integrity still passes) -> H1 still reports pass, overall=all-pass. selfcheck-m4.mjs check C (lines 156-177) only tests digests VALUE MISMATCH between records, never digests/goldMetrics ABSENCE, so this vacuous-pass path is untested.

Crash-on-missing-evidence contract violation: analyze-batch.mjs comment (lines 131-133) documents tamper-verdicts.jsonl as loaded best-effort where a missing required field yields inconclusive never a crash, and H2 (line 273) does handle tamperText==null by treating tamper as [] -> inconclusive. But main() at line 176 unconditionally calls readFileBytes(paths.tamper) again (unguarded readFileSync, no try/catch) to build generatedInputs['tamper-verdicts.jsonl']. If tamper-verdicts.jsonl is fully ABSENT (not just empty), this throws an uncaught ENOENT exception with a raw stack trace instead of the documented graceful inconclusive/no-crash behavior -- inconsistent with how resume-reconciliation.json (H3) is handled (readTextOrNull + graceful inconclusive), and inconsistent with the file's own stated contract. Reproduced by running analyze-batch.mjs in a sandbox with tamper-verdicts.jsonl deleted (all other evidence intact): process throws Error ENOENT at readFileBytes (analyze-batch.mjs:51) called from line 176, instead of writing an inconclusive report. selfcheck-m4.mjs check G (lines 250-264) only exercises an EMPTY resume-reconciliation.json, never an ABSENT tamper-verdicts.jsonl, so this crash path is untested. Not a false-pass (exit is nonzero, no report written) but a robustness/maintainability gap that contradicts the file's own documented never-crash-on-missing-tamper-evidence promise.

H4 lacks a sanity floor on elapsedMs: adjudicateH4 (analyze-batch.mjs:389-420) computes over = proofs.filter(r => !(r.elapsedMs <= cap)). A missing/undefined elapsedMs correctly fails (undefined <= cap is false), but a NEGATIVE elapsedMs (e.g. -999999, which is valid JSON and would survive a naive/buggy producer or a tamper of the ledger that re-signs recordDigest) silently satisfies elapsedMs <= cap and is counted as passing, with no lower-bound (>=0) check anywhere in H4. Reproduced: set one proof record's elapsedMs to -999999 and re-sign recordDigest (input-integrity passes) -> H4 verdict=pass, overall=all-pass (the SS3 claim gets asserted) despite a record carrying a nonsensical timing value that should at minimum be inconclusive/flagged, not silently pass. Contrast with H3, which uses strict === 0 equality (a -1 dupTotal correctly fails H3), so this is a narrow gap specific to H4's one-directional <= comparison. selfcheck-m4.mjs check F (lines 224-245) only tests elapsedMs ABOVE the cap, never a negative/sub-zero value, so this hole is untested.

F-CODEX-1 (host-2, HIGH): H1 COMPLETENESS false-pass. adjudicateH1 (analyze-batch.mjs:~221) requires only 'at least one scale with >=2 pairwise-equal records' to pass; a scale with FEWER records than protocol.N[scale] (e.g. only replay/full/1 present instead of the required 3) is marked non-checkable but does NOT prevent overall pass. So an incomplete campaign (missing full-scale replay evidence that protocol.N.full===3 demands) still yields H1 pass + overall all-pass + asserts the §3 claim. FIX: H1 must require EXACTLY protocol.N[scale] proof records per scale (completeness) before any scale is 'pass'; a short scale is fail or inconclusive, never silently ignored.

F-CODEX-2 (host-2, HIGH): H2 IDENTITY false-pass. adjudicateH2 (analyze-batch.mjs:~318) checks only per-disposition bucket COUNTS (18/2/6/1) + per-row conformance + dispositionMatch — NOT that each expected (class, handling) pair enumerated in protocol.tamperMatrix is actually PRESENT. Delete one class's verdict (e.g. gold-edit/raw) and duplicate another (cross-profile-swap/refreshed) so counts still total 18 fail-closed: H2 passes while an enumerated tamper class has ZERO evidence. FIX: H2 must verify the SET of (class,handling) identities in the verdicts equals the set enumerated in protocol.tamperMatrix (identity coverage), in addition to per-row conformance + dispositionMatch.

F-CODEX-3 (host-2, HIGH): H3 STUB false-pass. adjudicateH3 (analyze-batch.mjs:~356) checks only dupTotal===0 && gapTotal===0 && finalMultisetMatch===true. Replacing resume-reconciliation.json with the 3-field stub {dupTotal:0,gapTotal:0,finalMultisetMatch:true} passes even though the scored kill trials (killA/killB/killC), casualty dispositions, killC.stoppedRecordPreserved, and protocolReplaySmallCount evidence are ABSENT. FIX: H3 must validate the reconciliation carries its substantive evidence (killA/killB/killC objects each with dup/gap, protocolReplaySmallCount matching protocol.N.small, hypothesis field) — not just the 3 summary booleans.

F-CODEX-4 (host-2, MEDIUM; corroborates quality F-004): H4 accepts non-physical elapsedMs. adjudicateH4 (analyze-batch.mjs:~406) uses !(r.elapsedMs <= cap): a negative elapsedMs (-1) or null (coerced to 0 by <=) satisfies it and passes. FIX: require Number.isFinite(r.elapsedMs) && r.elapsedMs >= 0 && r.elapsedMs <= cap; a non-finite/negative elapsed is fail (not a valid scale-envelope datum).

H1 scale-loop only iterates scales declared in protocol.N (Object.keys(expectedN)), so a proof record at an undeclared/extra scale (e.g. a stray or injected record with garbage/vacuous digests+goldMetrics at a scale key not in protocol.N) is grouped into byScale[s] but never read by the perScale loop — it influences neither countOk/wellFormed/pairwiseEqual nor anyFail. Reproduced live: appended one extra ledger proof record at scale="bogus" (digests all "BAD", goldMetrics={}), re-signed its recordDigest so input-integrity passes, and analyze-batch.mjs still emitted overall=all-pass with H1=pass (report digest 3d8595534661b184f227e049b96cc3311e1007da50dca4b364d84e844b26fb87, distinct from the real all-pass digest). This violates H1s own stated criterion ("exactly N[s] proof records exist" / completeness) because there is no global check that proofs.length equals the sum of protocol.N values or that every proof.scale is a key of protocol.N — completeness is only verified per declared scale, not against the full evidence set. selfcheck-m4.mjs has no sub-check (A-O) covering an extra/undeclared-scale proof record, so this residual is unguarded. Recommend: H1 (or the input-integrity pre-check) should also require every proofs scale to be in protocol.N and/or that sum(perScale.n) === proofs.length, failing otherwise.

H3 false-pass: adjudicateH3/isKillWellFormed (experiments/pos-instrument-replay/analyze-batch.mjs:447-513) never checks killC.postResume.stoppedRecordPreserved. This is the specific substantive claim killC exists to prove per resume-reconciliation.json's own description ("killC additionally proves resume SKIPS an ALREADY-RECORDED verify_crash STOP ... the stop record preserved byte-identical"). Setting resume.killC.postResume.stoppedRecordPreserved=false (or deleting the field) still yields H3=pass and overall=all-pass (confirmed by direct repro against the committed evidence via a sandboxed copy of analyze-batch.mjs run against a mutated resume-reconciliation.json), so report.claim (the verbatim S3 text) is asserted even though the killC stop-record-preservation guarantee is falsified. isKillWellFormed only checks casualtyId+postResume+recordedBeforeKill are present keys on each kill object and never inspects the contents of postResume for killC. selfcheck-m4.mjs sub-checks J-O do not cover this field either (zero references to stoppedRecordPreserved in either analyze-batch.mjs or selfcheck-m4.mjs), so the new hermetic self-check suite does not catch it. This is exactly the attack named in the review brief (H3 substantive fields present but killC.stoppedRecordPreserved wrong).

H1 goldMetrics shape not validated: hasWellFormedProofEvidence (experiments/pos-instrument-replay/analyze-batch.mjs:251-260) only checks goldMetrics is a non-empty object, not that it carries any specific expected keys/shape. Replacing every proof record's goldMetrics with a uniform {bogus:1} (re-signed so integrity + pairwise-equality both hold) still yields H1=pass, overall=all-pass. The documented H1 criterion text explicitly only promises non-empty digests+goldMetrics (not specific goldMetrics keys), so this is arguably in-scope per the current spec rather than a regression — flagging as low severity for awareness/consideration, not as a blocking hardening gap, since fixing it would require deciding + documenting an expected goldMetrics schema (out of scope for this round's stated fix set).

F-CODEX-R2-1 (host-2, HIGH): H2 does not bind each (class,handling) identity to its PROTOCOL-EXPECTED disposition. adjudicateH2 checks the identity SET == protocol.tamperMatrix + aggregate per-disposition COUNTS + per-row conformance + dispositionMatch — but NOT that a given (class,handling) has the disposition the protocol assigns it. Swap cross-profile-swap|refreshed from fail-closed->accepted/pass AND gold-additive-field|refreshed from accepted->fail-closed/fail (keeping counts, dispositionMatch, fingerprintMatch all consistent): H2=pass, overall=all-pass. FIX: for each verdict, look up its (class,handling) in protocol.tamperMatrix, determine the EXPECTED bucket/disposition, and require rederivedDisposition === that expected disposition (identity->disposition binding), in addition to the existing set/count/conformance checks.

F-CODEX-R2-2 (host-2, HIGH; corroborates+extends quality F-010): H3 accepts false/empty nested resume evidence. adjudicateH3/isKillWellFormed requires only that killC.postResume exists as a key — it never inspects the substantive VALUES. Setting killC.postResume.stoppedRecordPreserved=false passes; replacing ALL kill*.postResume with {} also passes. FIX: H3 must validate the substantive kill-trial values: killC.postResume.stoppedRecordPreserved===true; each of killA/killB/killC postResume shows 0 dup / 0 gap and a resolved casualty disposition; reject an empty/false postResume.

F-CODEX-R2-3 (host-2, MEDIUM; corroborates quality F-011): H1 accepts partial goldMetrics. hasWellFormedProofEvidence requires goldMetrics to be a non-empty object but not the EXPECTED key set. Setting every proof record goldMetrics to {expectedIdsFoundRate:1} (re-signed) passes. FIX: require goldMetrics to carry the full expected metric key set (the keys the instrument's verify emits), not merely be non-empty.

dead-code: selfcheck-m4.mjs:594-599 checkQ has an empty no-op if-block (`if (e.countsMatch !== false) { /* comment only */ }`) that does nothing at runtime — should be deleted or replaced with a real assertion/console note; introduced in commit eeb1a9592
